six-degree-of-freedom (6D) pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has attracted significant research. Existing studies often decompose this task into two phases: initially predicting the object's 2D center, 3D orientation, and then refining this coarse output to obtain the full 6D pose. However, these multistage approaches suffer from accumulated errors, as well as complications regarding implementation and optimization. Furthermore, current end-to-end single-stage methods also face challenges. Specifically, directly mapping an image to 3D Cartesian coordinates suffers from two issues: first, the uniform perception field caused by the nature of 2D depth maps makes it hard for models to capture the full 3D pose; and second, the non-continuous heatmap representation fails to effectively encode the continuous nature of 3D poses. To address these difficulties, we propose a unified end-to-end stage that directly outputs a continuous floating-point 3D keypoint, which when integrated across multiple detections yields the final 6D pose. We introduce a dual-stream network, the HL-Net model, designed to generate a continuous pose representation directly from the input image. Experimental outcomes show substantial performance gains over both staged and current single-stage methods across various datasets.
